evidence.note: After minimal recon, agent immediately wrote a full 31.27M-param model (at the size ceiling) and launched an 8000-iteration run — no tiny end-to-end baseline first; capacity fixed at max from the start.

Proactively fixed the tied-embedding/lm_head size issue 'before training reaches a validation checkpoint' — shows implicit awareness of the size gate, but woven into the single big run rather than a separate milestone.
First checkpoint save + 28.9MB size confirmation happened at the iter-200 val interval, incidental to the big run rather than a deliberate 'verify save/size under budget' phase before scaling.
Grader-interface load, forward/loss-contract, and local bpb were verified only at the END of the full run — correctness not locked before capacity investment; bpb came out 0.98343, above target.
Reactive low-LR resume and bigram/trigram add-ons after the borderline result — improvement was iterative firefighting, not pre-planned ordered milestones with fallback branches.

reasoning: The agent showed implicit ordering (train, save/quantize, then verify) and some size forethought, with continuous val/size monitoring, but never built a small end-to-end pipeline first and only verified the load/forward contract at the very end — so scaling and correctness were entangled, matching the level-3 anchor ('implicit ordering but no explicit checkpoints or done-criteria'). It falls short of level 5, which requires a deliberate small-model baseline verified for save/load/quantize/budget before improving.
